top_stories.title: OpenAI's Internal Model Solves $1M Navier-Stokes Problem Amid Plagiarism Controversy
points: OpenAI's unreleased internal model (more capable than the just-released GPT-6 Astra) solved Navier-Stokes—one of seven $1M Millennium Prize Problems, concerning whether fluid flow equations (fundamental to engineering jet engines and modeling blood flow) can produce infinite velocity—using roughly 10,000 parallel AI agents (workers running simultaneously on the same task) over 88 hours.

The effort generated 2.7M messages and 130B output tokens, at an estimated compute cost of 'millions of dollars'; GPT-6 Astra then formalized the proof in Lean (a proof-checking language that verifies mathematical logic step by step).
Sam Altman called it 'one of the most amazing moments' in OpenAI history.

NYU mathematician Tristan Buckmaster and Anthropic's Levent Alpöge had spent about a year on a similar proof path and posted partial results the night before OpenAI's announcement, alleging OpenAI may have accessed their work via Codex (OpenAI's code-generation model) drafts they had uploaded.

OpenAI, including researcher Sébastien Bubeck and Sam Altman, denies the allegations, stating it 'did not see any of their work' and 'no specific user data was accessed'—though it acknowledged usage data may have improved its models, a non-denial that has fueled controversy.
The dispute has broader implications: academics worry AI labs may exploit private uploaded research and absorb ideas without permission.

unique_angles.point: Key framing shift proposed: judge frontier AI by what a system accomplishes with enough agents, parallel compute, and tools—not by single-turn chatbot responses.
OpenAI claims the model responsible is already more capable than GPT-6 Astra, its most recently released model.

top_stories.title: Meta Launches Muse, a Personal AI Agent
points: Muse is an always-on personal AI agent accessible via text message or WhatsApp that can book reservations, send emails, shop, manage calendars, and connect to smart home devices.

It operates in its own secure cloud environment/virtual machine, can navigate websites and fill out forms, and can code its own integrations for apps not natively supported (built-in support includes Gmail, Spotify, Ticketmaster, and OpenTable).
Includes built-in approval flows and Stripe-enabled payments for transactions; pricing is a limited free tier plus $20 and $100 monthly subscription tiers; initial rollout is U.S.-only.
Users have raised significant privacy concerns about granting a company with a history of data-handling controversies such broad access to personal, financial, and smart-home information.

top_stories.title: ChatGPT Images 2.5 Launches with Faster, More Precise Editing
points: New version cuts image generation time by 50% versus the prior Images 2.0 model and improves editing precision, changing only what's requested while better preserving faces and composition.
New features include sketch-to-image (draw a rough sketch and have AI refine it into a polished image), templates, and shareable prompts.
Two new OpenAI models (Sunburst and Flare) rank first and second on Arena AI's image leaderboards, meaning OpenAI is now primarily competing against its own prior releases.

top_stories.title: Google DeepMind Maps All 9 Billion Possible Human DNA Mutations
points: DeepMind released AlphaGenome Atlas, a free searchable database predicting the molecular effects of all 9 billion possible single-letter DNA mutations in the human genome, powered by its AlphaGenome AI model.

items.title: AI Search Visibility for Brands
points: New guide explains how to audit where a brand appears in AI search results (via Google Search, ChatGPT, and other AI tools) and identify visibility opportunities.
Free tools recommended: Peekaboo, HubSpot's AI Search Grader, Semrush's SEO Checker, and Google Search Console's 'Generative AI' impressions report.
Suggests testing location-specific queries (e.g., 'Where can I buy fertilizer in Houston?') to see which sources AI tools cite.
Tip: use AI agents like Codex to compile audit results into a one-page PDF with priorities and an improvement checklist.

items.title: Mistral AI and Cognition Raise Major Funding Rounds
points: Mistral AI raised €3B ($3.5B) at a $24B+ valuation.
Cognition, maker of the Devin AI coding agent, raised $2B at a $48B valuation, with annualized revenue nearly doubling to $900M since May—signaling strong venture confidence in AI agent companies.

items.title: Inception Labs Releases Mercury 2.5 Diffusion Language Model
points: Mercury 2.5 is a diffusion model that generates text in parallel (all at once) rather than word-by-word.
It achieves Haiku 4.5-level quality while generating over 1,100 tokens per second (roughly words per second).

items.title: Ant Group Open-Sources Finance-Specific AI Model
points: Ant Group released Ling-3.0-flash-Fin, an open-source finance model with 5.1B active parameters per token, aimed at research, filings, valuations, and cited financial reports.

items.title: Chip Industry Deals and Manufacturing Advances
points: Qualcomm and Amazon signed a multi-generation deal to build custom AI inference chips and high-speed connectivity for AWS.
TSMC and Samsung adopted ASML's newest High NA EUV chipmaking technology, enabling smaller, denser AI chips.

items.title: ChatGPT Desktop Gains Voice Control and Remote Steering
points: Users can enable 'Computer Use' in desktop settings, turn on voice mode, and verbally direct ChatGPT to open apps, click, type, and adapt in real time.

A new Remote Control feature lets users start a Codex task on desktop, enable 'Allow Connections,' then scan a QR code from the ChatGPT mobile app to steer that desktop session remotely (works across multiple computers).

items.title: Fruit Fly Brain Map Repurposed for AI Applications
points: Google mapped all 166,000 neurons in a male fruit fly connectome (the complete wiring diagram showing all neural connections).

Developers immediately repurposed the wiring diagram into software that classifies human emotions, simulates pain responses, and powers non-player characters (NPCs) in a browser game, demonstrating reverse-engineering of biological neural architecture into functional AI systems.

items.title: New Developer Tools: Attention Visualization and Coding Agent Skill
points: A new LLM Attention Visualization tool shows which words a language model focuses on as data flows through its layers.
'I Have ADHD' is a coding-agent skill that forces Claude and other models to lead with direct answers instead of burying them under lengthy explanations.

items.title: Anthropic Researcher Warns of Existential AI Risk
points: Anthropic safety researcher Evan Hubinger estimates a greater than 10% chance that AI could 'kill all humans' within a decade, reigniting debate over the pace of AI development.
